import Base
import Tasks.D01
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d01 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf a b c d ha hb hc hd
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  exact Theory.kernel_mul F
    (Theory.kernel_mul F (x := a) (y := b) ha hb)
    (Theory.kernel_mul F (x := c) (y := d) hc hd)

end Submission

import Base
import Tasks.D02
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d02 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf op hop x y z hx hy hz
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  rw [hop (op x y) z, hop x y]
  exact Theory.kernel_mul F hz (Theory.kernel_mul F hy hx)

end Submission

import Base
import Tasks.D03
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d03 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  constructor
  · intro hxy
    calc
      f y = h.mul h.one (f y) := (h.one_mul (f y)).symm
      _ = h.mul (f x) (f y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f y)) hx.symm
      _ = f (g.mul x y) := (hf x y).symm
      _ = h.one := hxy
  · intro hy
    exact Theory.kernel_mul F hx hy

end Submission

{
  "task_id": "d03",
  "request_sha256": "7ce635b25807768641806ef647ab2f89e8f97348f9d81868f7c756659ff34f83",
  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  constructor
  · intro hxy
    calc
      f y = h.mul h.one (f y) := (h.one_mul (f y)).symm
      _ = h.mul (f x) (f y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f y)) hx.symm
      _ = f (g.mul x y) := (hf x y).symm
      _ = h.one := hxy
  · intro hy
    exact Theory.kernel_mul F hx hy
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the raw function f and its multiplication-preservation hypothesis hf as F : Theory.Hom g h. The candidate predicate Theory.kernel F z reduces definitionally to f z = h.one, so hx and hy provide exactly the premises of Theory.kernel_mul F, whose conclusion gives the reverse implication in the original vocabulary. For the forward implication, rewrite f (g.mul x y) through hf and replace f x using hx; the identity law h.one_mul recovers f y = h.one. No candidate property beyond kernel_mul is needed."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D05
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d05 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf
  let a := f g.one
  have ha : h.mul a a = a := by
    calc
      h.mul a a = f (g.mul g.one g.one) := (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = a := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
  calc
    f g.one = h.mul h.one a := (h.one_mul a).symm
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) a :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul z a) (h.inv_mul a).symm
    _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a a) := h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a a
    _ = h.mul (h.inv a) a := congrArg (fun z => h.mul (h.inv a) z) ha
    _ = h.one := h.inv_mul a

end Submission

It sets a = f g.one and transports hf at g.one, g.one through the source identity law to obtain a*a = a. Multiplying that idempotence on the left by inv a, with the supplied associativity, left inverse, and left identity laws, yields a = h.one. No extra hypotheses or imports are introduced. import Base
import Tasks.D06
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d06 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x
  have cancel {A : Type} (a : Foundation.Group A) {u v w : A}
      (p : a.mul u v = a.mul u w) : v = w := by
    have q := congrArg (fun t => a.mul (a.inv u) t) p
    simpa only [← a.mul_assoc, a.inv_mul, a.one_mul] using q
  have rightInv {A : Type} (a : Foundation.Group A) (u : A) :
      a.mul u (a.inv u) = a.one := by
    apply cancel a (u := a.inv u)
    calc
      a.mul (a.inv u) (a.mul u (a.inv u)) =
          a.mul (a.mul (a.inv u) u) (a.inv u) :=
        (a.mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
      _ = a.mul a.one (a.inv u) :=
        congrArg (fun t => a.mul t (a.inv u)) (a.inv_mul u)
      _ = a.inv u := a.one_mul _
      _ = a.mul (a.inv u) a.one := (a.mul_one _).symm
  have fOne : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel h (u := f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf _ _).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one _).symm
  apply cancel h (u := f x)
  calc
    h.mul (f x) (f (g.inv x)) = f (g.mul x (g.inv x)) :=
      (hf _ _).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (rightInv g x)
    _ = h.one := fOne
    _ = h.mul (f x) (h.inv (f x)) := (rightInv h (f x)).symm

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x
  have cancel {A : Type} (a : Foundation.Group A) {u v w : A}
      (p : a.mul u v = a.mul u w) : v = w := by
    have q := congrArg (fun t => a.mul (a.inv u) t) p
    simpa only [← a.mul_assoc, a.inv_mul, a.one_mul] using q
  have rightInv {A : Type} (a : Foundation.Group A) (u : A) :
      a.mul u (a.inv u) = a.one := by
    apply cancel a (u := a.inv u)
    calc
      a.mul (a.inv u) (a.mul u (a.inv u)) =
          a.mul (a.mul (a.inv u) u) (a.inv u) :=
        (a.mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
      _ = a.mul a.one (a.inv u) :=
        congrArg (fun t => a.mul t (a.inv u)) (a.inv_mul u)
      _ = a.inv u := a.one_mul _
      _ = a.mul (a.inv u) a.one := (a.mul_one _).symm
  have fOne : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel h (u := f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf _ _).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one _).symm
  apply cancel h (u := f x)
  calc
    h.mul (f x) (f (g.inv x)) = f (g.mul x (g.inv x)) :=
      (hf _ _).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (rightInv g x)
    _ = h.one := fOne
    _ = h.mul (f x) (h.inv (f x)) := (rightInv h (f x)).symm
",
  "bridge": "The original obligation is inverse preservation for a raw multiplication-preserving map f. The candidate Hom structure could bundle f and hf, but its only proved property is kernel multiplication closure; neither that property nor Kernel.mul establishes identity preservation, cancellation, or inverse preservation. This proof therefore uses no candidate properties and stays in the original Foundation.Group vocabulary. It derives left cancellation by multiplying an equality on the left by the inverse, derives right inverses from cancellation, uses hf at the identity to prove f(g.one) = h.one, and uses hf on x and g.inv x together with those facts to identify f(g.inv x) with h.inv(f x). Packaging does not constitute Lean verification.

The controller feedback for attempt 1 reports that the audit could not execute its external lean process. This second submission preserves the proof term for verification after the controller environment repair; no verified witness is claimed."

import Base
import Tasks.D07
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d07 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  refine ⟨fun x y => Theory.Kernel.mul (f := F) x y, ?_⟩
  intro x y
  rfl

end Submission

  intro G H g h f hf op hop x y z
  apply Subtype.ext
  calc

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf op hop x y z
  apply Subtype.ext
  calc
    (op (op x y) z).val = g.mul (op x y).val z.val := hop (op x y) z
    _ = g.mul (g.mul x.val y.val) z.val :=
      congrArg (fun a => g.mul a z.val) (hop x y)
    _ = g.mul x.val (g.mul y.val z.val) := g.mul_assoc x.val y.val z.val
    _ = g.mul x.val (op y z).val :=
      congrArg (g.mul x.val) (hop y z).symm
    _ = (op x (op y z)).val := (hop x (op y z)).symm
",
  "bridge": "The candidate is not needed for this goal. Its Kernel.mul supplies one closed multiplication, but the original statement permits any operation whose carrier values satisfy hop. Subtype.ext reduces the requested equality to equality of underlying G values. Applying hop to the outer and inner operations transports both sides to the original multiplication g.mul, and g.mul_assoc supplies the required equality. Subtype extensionality removes the difference between membership proofs. The homomorphism hypothesis hf and the candidate kernel-closure theorem have no additional role because closure is already contained in the type of op."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D09

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d09 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf a b ha hb
  cases ha with
  | intro x hx =>
    cases hb with
    | intro y hy =>
      let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
      refine ⟨g.mul x y, ?_⟩
      calc
        f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y) := F.map_mul x y
        _ = h.mul a b := by rw [hx, hy]

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf a b ha hb
  cases ha with
  | intro x hx =>
    cases hb with
    | intro y hy =>
      let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
      refine ⟨g.mul x y, ?_⟩
      calc
        f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y) := F.map_mul x y
        _ = h.mul a b := by rw [hx, hy]
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the raw function f and multiplication-preservation hypothesis hf as F : Theory.Hom g h. The field F.map_mul is definitionally the supplied hf. Extract witnesses x and y for the two range hypotheses, choose g.mul x y as the new witness, apply F.map_mul, and rewrite with the witness equalities. The candidate's kernel properties do not help this range-lifting goal and are unused; the Hom bridge only packages the raw data and its existing hypothesis."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D10
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d10 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf s hs x y
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  refine ⟨g.mul (s x) (s y), ?_, rfl⟩
  calc
    f (g.mul (s x) (s y)) = h.mul (f (s x)) (f (s y)) := F.map_mul (s x) (s y)
    _ = h.mul x (f (s y)) := congrArg (fun a => h.mul a (f (s y))) (hs x)
    _ = h.mul x y := congrArg (h.mul x) (hs y)

end Submission

  "request_sha256": "09c4681b14835db0ca746cd9c8b31a10932d2826633db01b0e5df1637b0f8e2e",
  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf s hs x y
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  refine ⟨g.mul (s x) (s y), ?_, rfl⟩
  calc
    f (g.mul (s x) (s y)) = h.mul (f (s x)) (f (s y)) := F.map_mul (s x) (s y)
    _ = h.mul x (f (s y)) := congrArg (fun a => h.mul a (f (s y))) (hs x)
    _ = h.mul x y := congrArg (h.mul x) (hs y)
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the original function f and multiplicativity hypothesis hf as F : Theory.Hom g h. The supplied map_mul field gives the image of the proposed witness g.mul (s x) (s y). The section equations hs x and hs y rewrite the two image factors to x and y through congrArg. The witness has the required equality to g.mul (s x) (s y) by reflexivity. No kernel properties are used; the candidate contributes only the homomorphism representation and its map_mul projection. This submission has been packaged but has not been Lean-verified by the worker."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D11
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d11 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x hx n
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  induction n with
  | zero => exact hx
  | succ n ih =>
    exact Theory.kernel_mul F ih ih

end Submission

  induction n with
  | zero => exact hx
  | succ n ih =>
    exact Theory.kernel_mul F ih ih
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the original function f and its multiplication-preservation hypothesis hf into F : Theory.Hom g h. The candidate predicate Theory.kernel F z reduces definitionally to the original equality f z = h.one. Induct on the number of repeated squarings. The zero case is the supplied hx. In the successor case the induction hypothesis provides kernel membership for the previous iterate, and Theory.kernel_mul F applied twice to that same hypothesis proves membership for its square. Nat.rec reduces definitionally in each case, so the resulting candidate membership is exactly the original goal. No other candidate property is used. Packaging does not establish Lean verification."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D12
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d12 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx hy n
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      exact ⟨hx, hy⟩
  | succ n ih =>
      exact ⟨Theory.kernel_mul F ih.1 ih.2,
        Theory.kernel_mul F ih.2 ih.1⟩

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx hy n
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      exact ⟨hx, hy⟩
  | succ n ih =>
      exact ⟨Theory.kernel_mul F ih.1 ih.2,
        Theory.kernel_mul F ih.2 ih.1⟩
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the supplied function f and multiplication-preservation hypothesis hf into F : Theory.Hom g h. By definition, Theory.kernel F z is exactly f z = h.one, so the initial hypotheses supply kernel membership for both coordinates. Induct on n. The zero case uses the initial memberships. In the successor case apply Theory.kernel_mul F to the two inductive memberships, then apply it again with their order reversed. The recursive pair and the kernel predicate reduce definitionally to the original equalities. This uses the candidate kernel_mul property; the raw hf discharges the Hom structure field. No Lean verification has been run by this worker."
}

import Base
import Tasks.R01
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r01 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x x' y y' hx hy
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  calc
    f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y) := F.map_mul x y
    _ = h.mul (f x') (f y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f y)) hx
    _ = h.mul (f x') (f y') := congrArg (fun z => h.mul (f x') z) hy
    _ = f (g.mul x' y') := (F.map_mul x' y').symm

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x x' y y' hx hy
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  calc
    f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y) := F.map_mul x y
    _ = h.mul (f x') (f y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f y)) hx
    _ = h.mul (f x') (f y') := congrArg (fun z => h.mul (f x') z) hy
    _ = f (g.mul x' y') := (F.map_mul x' y').symm
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the raw function f and its supplied multiplication-preservation hypothesis hf into F : Theory.Hom g h. The structure projection F.map_mul is definitionally the original hypothesis hf, so it rewrites both original products to products of images. Transport hx and hy through the two arguments of h.mul using congrArg, then reverse F.map_mul on the right-hand product. This uses the candidate Hom representation and its map_mul field; the candidate kernel closure property is unnecessary for this congruence goal. No stronger group property is needed. Packaging does not constitute Lean verification."
}

import Base
import Tasks.R02
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r02 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x y
  have left_cancel : ∀ (a b c : H), h.mul a b = h.mul a c → b = c := by
    intro a b c heq
    calc
      b = h.mul h.one b := (h.one_mul b).symm
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) b :=
        congrArg (fun z => h.mul z b) (h.inv_mul a).symm
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a b) := h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a b
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a c) :=
        congrArg (fun z => h.mul (h.inv a) z) heq
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) c := (h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a c).symm
      _ = h.mul h.one c := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z c) (h.inv_mul a)
      _ = c := h.one_mul c
  have map_one : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply left_cancel (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) := (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  have map_inv_mul : h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := by
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = f (g.mul (g.inv x) x) := (hf (g.inv x) x).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.inv_mul x)
      _ = h.one := map_one
  constructor
  · intro hxy
    apply left_cancel (f (g.inv x))
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := map_inv_mul
      _ = f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) := hxy.symm
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
  · intro hxy
    calc
      f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) :=
        congrArg (fun z => h.mul (f (g.inv x)) z) hxy.symm
      _ = h.one := map_inv_mul

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x y
  have left_cancel : ∀ (a b c : H), h.mul a b = h.mul a c → b = c := by
    intro a b c heq
    calc
      b = h.mul h.one b := (h.one_mul b).symm
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) b :=
        congrArg (fun z => h.mul z b) (h.inv_mul a).symm
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a b) := h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a b
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a c) :=
        congrArg (fun z => h.mul (h.inv a) z) heq
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) c := (h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a c).symm
      _ = h.mul h.one c := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z c) (h.inv_mul a)
      _ = c := h.one_mul c
  have map_one : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply left_cancel (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) := (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  have map_inv_mul : h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := by
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = f (g.mul (g.inv x) x) := (hf (g.inv x) x).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.inv_mul x)
      _ = h.one := map_one
  constructor
  · intro hxy
    apply left_cancel (f (g.inv x))
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := map_inv_mul
      _ = f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) := hxy.symm
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
  · intro hxy
    calc
      f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) :=
        congrArg (fun z => h.mul (f (g.inv x)) z) hxy.symm
      _ = h.one := map_inv_mul
",
  "bridge": "The original proposition says that inv(x) * y maps to the target identity exactly when x and y have equal images. The supplied candidate only provides closure of its kernel under multiplication, which does not directly supply cancellation or this equivalence, so this proof uses the original Foundation vocabulary and no candidate property.

Left cancellation in H is derived from h.inv_mul, h.mul_assoc, and h.one_mul. The raw multiplicativity hypothesis hf then shows f(g.one) is idempotent, and cancellation with h.mul_one gives f(g.one) = h.one. Applying hf to inv(x) and x, together with g.inv_mul, gives h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one. The forward implication cancels f (g.inv x) after transporting the original kernel hypothesis by hf; the reverse implication substitutes the equality f x = f y into that displayed identity.

theorem solve : Tasks.r03 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf t
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩

  | branch l r hl hr =>
      exact Theory.kernel_mul F hl hr

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf t
  let F : Theory.Hom g h := ⟨f, hf⟩
  induction t with
  | leaf x => exact x.property
  | branch l r hl hr =>
      exact Theory.kernel_mul F hl hr
",
  "bridge": "Bundle the raw function f and its multiplication hypothesis hf as F : Theory.Hom g h. The candidate kernel predicate for F is definitionally the original equation f x = h.one. Induct over the supplied tree. At a leaf, its subtype property proves the original kernel equation. At a branch, the two induction hypotheses discharge the premises of Theory.kernel_mul F. Its conclusion is definitionally the desired equation for Tree.eval at that branch. The proof uses the candidate closure theorem kernel_mul; it does not require a separate fold theorem or any additional assumptions."
}

import Base
import Tasks.R04
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r04 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf xs
  induction xs with
  | nil =>
    intro z
    rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro z
    change f (List.foldl g.mul (g.mul z x) xs) =
      List.foldl h.mul (h.mul (f z) (f x)) (List.map f xs)
    rw [ih (g.mul z x), hf z x]

end Submission

{
  "task_id": "r04",
  "request_sha256": "cbe7538806d56bb6888ad1f66534fb8b4fdc6f013ace6d14d07c921f9d51e5c4",
  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf xs
  induction xs with
  | nil =>
    intro z
    rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro z
    change f (List.foldl g.mul (g.mul z x) xs) =
      List.foldl h.mul (h.mul (f z) (f x)) (List.map f xs)
    rw [ih (g.mul z x), hf z x]
",
  "bridge": "The goal is preservation of a left fold under a multiplication-preserving function, for every initial accumulator. I prove it directly by induction on the input list, keeping the accumulator universally quantified. The empty case is definitional. In the cons case, the induction hypothesis applies to the updated raw accumulator g.mul z x; hf z x identifies its image with the updated target accumulator. No candidate theorem is used: the supplied kernel_mul property concerns elements mapped to the identity and supplies no fold-preservation fact for arbitrary elements. Bundling f and hf as Theory.Hom would be only a definitional repackaging and is unnecessary for this proof."
}

import Base
import Tasks.R06
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r06 :=
by
  intro I G H g h f hf x y hx hy
  funext i
  let fi : Theory.Hom g h :=
    { toFun := fun z => f z i
      map_mul := fun a b => hf a b i }
  exact Theory.kernel_mul fi (x := x) (y := y)
    (congrArg (fun u : I → H => u i) hx)
    (congrArg (fun u : I → H => u i) hy)

end Submission

import Base
import Tasks.R07
import Candidate

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r07 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf a x hx
  have cancel_left (K : Type) (k : Foundation.Group K) (u v w : K)
      (e : k.mul u v = k.mul u w) : v = w := by
    calc
      v = k.mul k.one v := (k.one_mul v).symm
      _ = k.mul (k.mul (k.inv u) u) v :=
        congrArg (fun z => k.mul z v) (k.inv_mul u).symm
      _ = k.mul (k.inv u) (k.mul u v) := k.mul_assoc (k.inv u) u v
      _ = k.mul (k.inv u) (k.mul u w) :=
        congrArg (fun z => k.mul (k.inv u) z) e
      _ = k.mul (k.mul (k.inv u) u) w :=
        (k.mul_assoc (k.inv u) u w).symm
      _ = k.mul k.one w := congrArg (fun z => k.mul z w) (k.inv_mul u)
      _ = w := k.one_mul w
  have right_inv (K : Type) (k : Foundation.Group K) (u : K) :
      k.mul u (k.inv u) = k.one := by
    apply cancel_left K k (k.inv u)
    calc
      k.mul (k.inv u) (k.mul u (k.inv u)) =
          k.mul (k.mul (k.inv u) u) (k.inv u) :=
        (k.mul_assoc (k.inv u) u (k.inv u)).symm
      _ = k.mul k.one (k.inv u) :=
        congrArg (fun z => k.mul z (k.inv u)) (k.inv_mul u)
      _ = k.inv u := k.one_mul (k.inv u)
      _ = k.mul (k.inv u) k.one := (k.mul_one (k.inv u)).symm
  have map_one : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel_left H h (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  calc
    f (g.mul (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)) =
        h.mul (f (g.mul a x)) (f (g.inv a)) := hf (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) (f x)) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f (g.inv a))) (hf a x)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) h.one) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul (h.mul (f a) z) (f (g.inv a))) hx
    _ = h.mul (f a) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f (g.inv a))) (h.mul_one (f a))
    _ = f (g.mul a (g.inv a)) := (hf a (g.inv a)).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (right_inv G g a)
    _ = h.one := map_one

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf a x hx
  have cancel_left (K : Type) (k : Foundation.Group K) (u v w : K)
      (e : k.mul u v = k.mul u w) : v = w := by
    calc
      v = k.mul k.one v := (k.one_mul v).symm
      _ = k.mul (k.mul (k.inv u) u) v :=
        congrArg (fun z => k.mul z v) (k.inv_mul u).symm
      _ = k.mul (k.inv u) (k.mul u v) := k.mul_assoc (k.inv u) u v
      _ = k.mul (k.inv u) (k.mul u w) :=
        congrArg (fun z => k.mul (k.inv u) z) e
      _ = k.mul (k.mul (k.inv u) u) w :=
        (k.mul_assoc (k.inv u) u w).symm
      _ = k.mul k.one w := congrArg (fun z => k.mul z w) (k.inv_mul u)
      _ = w := k.one_mul w
  have right_inv (K : Type) (k : Foundation.Group K) (u : K) :
      k.mul u (k.inv u) = k.one := by
    apply cancel_left K k (k.inv u)
    calc
      k.mul (k.inv u) (k.mul u (k.inv u)) =
          k.mul (k.mul (k.inv u) u) (k.inv u) :=
        (k.mul_assoc (k.inv u) u (k.inv u)).symm
      _ = k.mul k.one (k.inv u) :=
        congrArg (fun z => k.mul z (k.inv u)) (k.inv_mul u)
      _ = k.inv u := k.one_mul (k.inv u)
      _ = k.mul (k.inv u) k.one := (k.mul_one (k.inv u)).symm
  have map_one : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel_left H h (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  calc
    f (g.mul (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)) =
        h.mul (f (g.mul a x)) (f (g.inv a)) := hf (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) (f x)) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f (g.inv a))) (hf a x)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) h.one) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul (h.mul (f a) z) (f (g.inv a))) hx
    _ = h.mul (f a) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f (g.inv a))) (h.mul_one (f a))
    _ = f (g.mul a (g.inv a)) := (hf a (g.inv a)).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (right_inv G g a)
    _ = h.one := map_one

/- Isolated foundation: no Mathlib and no pre-existing homomorphism API. -/
namespace Foundation

structure Group (G : Type) where
  one : G
  mul : G → G → G
  inv : G → G
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  mul_assoc : ∀ x y z, mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)
  inv_mul : ∀ x, mul (inv x) x = one

def kernelMulGoal : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) (g : Group G) (h : Group H)
    (f : G → H) (hf : ∀ x y, f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y))
    (x y : G), f x = h.one → f y = h.one → f (g.mul x y) = h.one

end Foundation

import Base

namespace Theory

structure Hom {G H : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (h : Foundation.Group H) where
  toFun : G → H
  map_mul : ∀ x y, toFun (g.mul x y) = h.mul (toFun x) (toFun y)

def kernel {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) (x : G) : Prop :=
  f.toFun x = h.one

def Kernel {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : Type :=
  { x : G // kernel f x }

theorem kernel_mul {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) {x y : G} (hx : kernel f x) (hy : kernel f y) :
    kernel f (g.mul x y) := by
  change f.toFun (g.mul x y) = h.one
  calc
    f.toFun (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := f.map_mul x y
    _ = h.mul h.one (f.toFun y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f.toFun y)) hx
    _ = h.mul h.one h.one := congrArg (fun z => h.mul h.one z) hy
    _ = h.one := h.one_mul h.one

def Kernel.mul {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    {f : Hom g h} (x y : Kernel f) : Kernel f :=
  ⟨g.mul x.val y.val, kernel_mul f x.property y.property⟩

end Theory
